choices: every non-trivial property of the behavior (the function or language computed) of a program is undecidable
every property of a program's source-code syntax is undecidable
no program can print its own source code
every decidable problem is also semi-decidable
explanation: Rice's theorem: any non-trivial property of the partial function (behavior) computed by a program is undecidable, proved by reduction from HALT. Option B is false — syntactic properties such as 'does the source have five lines?' are decidable; Rice concerns semantic/behavioral properties. Option C is refuted by quines (recursion theorem); option D, though true, is not Rice's theorem.
